evals.prompt: Which of our pages are stuck on page two of Google?
evals.expected_output: Should run seo_report with section second-page (or `seo report --section second-page`). Should describe the rows as pages with an average position of 11 to 20 and their queries. Should offer seo_page for one page's queries and live facts as the next step.
assertions: Runs the second-page section of the report
Describes rows as pages at average positions 11 to 20 with their queries
Offers seo_page or `seo page` as the next step

evals.prompt: Agent task: second-page section for sc-domain:example.com from 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-28, then the next page of rows after the first 20.
evals.expected_output: Should run seo_report with site sc-domain:example.com, section second-page, start_date 2026-08-01 and end_date 2026-08-28 (or the CLI flags --start-date and --end-date). Should then request detail rows with offset 20 for the same window. Should not add parameters the tool does not define.
assertions: Runs the second-page section with both start and end dates
Requests detail rows with offset 20 for the next page
Keeps the same date window for the second call

evals.prompt: The second-page section came back empty, so nothing on our site needs work. Agreed?
evals.expected_output: Should not treat an empty section as an all-clear. Should check the date window and any limits the result names, and note that an empty section only means no pages met the rule in that window. Should suggest looking at the other section counts in the main report.
assertions: Does not treat the empty section as an all-clear
Checks the date window and limits in the result
Suggests other sections of the main report
